tasks.spec:
You are wiring an existing, tested safety component into the caller that ignores it. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps; this task needs neither.

YOU OWN EXACTLY THREE FILES:
  1. server/pipeline/contact_index.py   (create it)
  2. scripts/guest_candidate_feed.py    (edit it)
  3. fix-summary.md                     (create it)

Touching any other file fails the check. In particular do NOT edit server/pipeline/contact_state.py or anything under server/pipeline/contact_sources/ — they are finished and verified.

## The problem, precisely

scripts/guest_candidate_feed.py decides who receives a COLD FIRST-CONTACT email. On 2026-08-10 it came one review verdict away from sending a 'want to come on the show?' template to somebody already mid-conversation with the owner, because the only place it looked was a ledger field that happened to be empty.

The fix was built: server/pipeline/contact_state.py resolves 'have we already talked to this person' from observed evidence, and four adapters under server/pipeline/contact_sources/ (gmail_source, linkedin_source, bee_source, hubspot_source) report what each channel saw. READ contact_state.py FIRST — its module docstring is the authority model and you must not re-derive it. Then skim one adapter, e.g. gmail_source.py, for the interface.

Nothing calls any of it. That is your job. Run this right now to see today's actual behaviour, with every contact credential stripped from the environment:

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u15_contact_gate_check.py --worktree "$PWD"

It selects a candidate for outreach having consulted no contact channel at all.

## File 1: server/pipeline/contact_index.py

One read of every channel per run, then one verdict per person.

    SOURCES = (gmail_source, linkedin_source, bee_source, hubspot_source)   # module objects

    class ContactIndex:            # a dataclass is fine
        observations: dict[str, list[Observation]]   # alias -> every source's observations
        coverage: list[SourceCoverage]               # one entry per source attempted
        def resolve(self, alias, extra_observations=()) -> ContactVerdict

    def build(people, *, sources=None, now=None) -> ContactIndex

`people` is a list of {"alias": str, "name": str, "email": str or None}. `sources` defaults to SOURCES and is the injection seam the check uses — honour it exactly, including source modules that are plain objects exposing only SOURCE_NAME and observe(people, *, client=None, now=None).

build() calls each source's observe(people, now=now), merges the returned observations by alias (never dropping one source's observation because another also reported), and collects one coverage entry per source.

THE RULE THAT CARRIES THE SAFETY: if a source module raises — any exception, including at import or attribute lookup — build() must NOT propagate it and must NOT skip the source. It records SourceCoverage(source=<name>, reached=False, checked_at=<tz-aware now>, detail="<one line: why>"). A channel that was never read must look different from a channel with nothing in it. If it does not, the resolver clears a cold email to somebody we mailed last week.

resolve(alias, extra_observations=()) returns contact_state.resolve(<this alias's observations> + <extra_observations>, self.coverage). Do not reimplement the resolution logic; call it.

## File 2: scripts/guest_candidate_feed.py

Change build_candidates to:

    def build_candidates(inbox, ledger, now, limit, *, contact_index=None)

Keep the four positional arguments exactly as they are — other callers pass them positionally. contact_index is keyword-only and defaults to None, meaning 'build the real one'.

Order of operations matters:

  1. Run the existing cheap filters unchanged (non-object, no name, no email, ledger hold, excluded stage, inside the cadence floor). Those drops keep their current reasons.
  2. Build the people list from ONLY the survivors — alias, name, email — and, if contact_index is None, call contact_index.build(people). A contact lookup discloses somebody's address to up to four external systems; never run one for a record already dropped.
  3. For each survivor, assemble its SECOND-ORDER observations and pass them as extra_observations:
       * the intake note. The existing note_indicates_prior_contact() marker becomes contact_state.Observation(source="funnel_ledger", at=None, grounding=<the marker>, evidence_ref="funnel-ledger:<alias>"). KEEP the helper and its docstring; it stops being a decision and becomes evidence.
       * the ledger's last_touch. If the ledger records a touch that survived the cadence filter (an older one), that is a recording of contact too — same shape, grounded in the ledger, with its parsed timestamp if you have one.
  4. Call contact_index.resolve(alias, extra_observations=...). Select ONLY when verdict.safe_for_cold_open is true. Everyone else is dropped with a reason naming, in plain words, the VERDICT (the literal word UNKNOWN or CONTACTED), the source that saw the touch when there is one, and the unreached channels by name when there are any. Put the machine-readable verdict on the drop entry as well.
  5. Add a top-level "contact_coverage" block to the report: per source, reached and detail. Without it a run where three of four channels were unreadable reviews identically to a healthy one.

PRIVACY, enforced by the check: the report names records by ALIAS only. No name, no email address, no note text, ever — including inside a drop reason. Say 'the intake note reports an exchange already under way', never the note itself.

Delete nothing else. The drop accounting, the private 0600 writes, the report-before-candidates write order and invite_copy() all stay as they are.

## Two ways to fake this task, both of which the check catches

  * Holding everybody. A gate that never clears passes every safety scenario and is an outage wearing a safety receipt. A person with all four channels read and genuinely no history MUST still be selected.
  * Keeping the old string guard as the real decision and calling the resolver decoratively. The check asserts the note reaches the resolver as a second-order observation carrying grounding.

## Run the exact check until it prints PASS

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u15_contact_gate_check.py --worktree "$PWD"

It drives build() with an exploding source, drives build_candidates with injected coverage pictures, and runs the real CLI with every credential stripped. Read its failure text; it says exactly what is wrong.

## fix-summary.md

Three sections, using these words as headings: 'What changed', 'How I verified', 'Risk'. Under 'How I verified' paste the actual final output of the check command. Under 'Risk' state what happens in production TODAY given that gmail, linkedin and hubspot credentials are not present in the feeder's environment. Under 400 words.
tasks.verified: Executes the candidate feeder against controlled pictures of contact history and through its real command line. Incomplete coverage must hold, a first-order touch must hold, an intake note and an uncorroborated ledger row must hold, and a fully-covered genuinely empty history must still clear — that last one is what stops a worker from passing by refusing everybody. The drop report must name the verdict and the unreached channels while naming no person, and the shipped CLI run with every contact credential removed must select nobody and say why.
